spec.title: Earthquakes — the last 30 days
spec.description: Earthquakes from the USGS feed over the last 30 days, with who lives nearby.

source.sql:
SELECT
  f.id AS id,
  to_timestamp(f.properties.time / 1000) AS time,
  f.geometry.coordinates[2]::DOUBLE AS latitude,
  f.geometry.coordinates[1]::DOUBLE AS longitude,
  f.geometry.coordinates[3]::DOUBLE AS depth,
  f.properties.mag::DOUBLE AS mag,
  f.properties.place::VARCHAR AS place,
  f.properties.alert::VARCHAR AS alert,
  f.properties.mmi::DOUBLE AS mmi,
  f.properties.felt::INTEGER AS felt,
  f.properties.tsunami::INTEGER AS tsunami,
  f.properties.sig::INTEGER AS sig,
  f.properties.url::VARCHAR AS url
FROM read_json('https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/summary/all_month.geojson'), unnest(features) AS t(f)
WHERE f.properties.mag IS NOT NULL

SELECT
  f.properties.name::VARCHAR AS name,
  f.properties.adm0name::VARCHAR AS country,
  f.properties.latitude::DOUBLE AS latitude,
  f.properties.longitude::DOUBLE AS longitude,
  f.properties.pop_min::BIGINT AS pop_min,
  f.properties.pop_max::BIGINT AS pop_max
FROM read_json('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/v5.1.2/geojson/ne_10m_populated_places_simple.geojson'), unnest(features) AS t(f)
WHERE f.properties.pop_min > 0

WITH q AS (
  SELECT id, latitude, longitude FROM $quakes WHERE mag >= 4.5
),
near AS (
  -- A band of about 111 km around each quake first, so the distance runs on
  -- a few candidates instead of every place on Earth. The longitude band
  -- widens with latitude and wraps at the antimeridian.
  SELECT q.id, p.name, p.pop_min, p.pop_max,
         2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(
           power(sin(radians(p.latitude - q.latitude) / 2), 2)
           + cos(radians(q.latitude)) * cos(radians(p.latitude))
             * power(sin(radians(p.longitude - q.longitude) / 2), 2)
         )) AS km
  FROM q
  JOIN $places AS p
    ON p.latitude BETWEEN q.latitude - 1 AND q.latitude + 1
   AND least(abs(p.longitude - q.longitude), 360 - abs(p.longitude - q.longitude))
       <= 1 / greatest(cos(radians(q.latitude)), 0.01)
)
SELECT q.id,
       -- DOUBLE, not BIGINT: DuckDB promotes SUM(BIGINT) to HUGEINT, which
       -- DuckDB-WASM serializes as a part-indexed object, not a JS number, in
       -- any consumer that sums this column across rows.
       coalesce(sum(n.pop_min) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100), 0)::DOUBLE AS people_100km,
       count(n.name) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100) AS places_100km,
       arg_max(n.name, n.pop_max) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100) AS largest_place,
       max(n.pop_max) FILTER (WHERE n.km <= 100) AS largest_pop
FROM q
LEFT JOIN near AS n ON n.id = q.id
GROUP BY q.id

spec.rawSql:
WITH area AS (
  SELECT
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
  FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($quakeArea, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
)
SELECT count(*) AS "Earthquakes"
FROM $quakes, area
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
  AND time >= coalesce(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
AND time < coalesce(try_cast($quakeTo AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
  AND mag >= coalesce(try_cast($mag_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND mag < coalesce(try_cast($mag_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) >= coalesce(try_cast($depth_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) < coalesce(try_cast($depth_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)

spec.title: Earthquakes and populated places
spec.description: Earthquakes of the last 30 days from the USGS feed, sized by magnitude, over populated places from Natural Earth. Drag the time slider or draw an area to filter the rest of the dashboard; click an earthquake to see who lives near it.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT id, time, latitude, longitude, mag, depth, place, alert
FROM $quakes
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
  AND mag >= coalesce(try_cast($mag_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND mag < coalesce(try_cast($mag_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) >= coalesce(try_cast($depth_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) < coalesce(try_cast($depth_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)

SELECT name, country, latitude, longitude, pop_max
FROM $places
WHERE pop_max >= 100000

spec.title: Magnitude
spec.description: Drag across the bars to filter the dashboard by magnitude. Grey is every earthquake in the time range; colour is what the other filters leave.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT floor(mag / 0.5) * 0.5 AS bin, count(*) AS n
FROM $quakes
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH area AS (
  SELECT
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
  FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($quakeArea, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
)
SELECT floor(mag / 0.5) * 0.5 AS bin, count(*) AS n
FROM $quakes, area
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
  AND time >= coalesce(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
AND time < coalesce(try_cast($quakeTo AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
  AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) >= coalesce(try_cast($depth_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) < coalesce(try_cast($depth_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

spec.title: Depth (km)
spec.description: Drag across the bars to filter the dashboard by depth. Grey is every earthquake in the time range; colour is what the other filters leave. Depths beyond 300 km are counted in the last bar.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT floor(greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) / 10) * 10 AS bin, count(*) AS n
FROM $quakes
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH area AS (
  SELECT
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
  FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($quakeArea, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
)
SELECT floor(greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) / 10) * 10 AS bin, count(*) AS n
FROM $quakes, area
WHERE $__timeFilter(time)
  AND time >= coalesce(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
AND time < coalesce(try_cast($quakeTo AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
  AND mag >= coalesce(try_cast($mag_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND mag < coalesce(try_cast($mag_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE)
  AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH area AS (
  SELECT
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
  FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($quakeArea, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
), f AS (
  SELECT q.* FROM $quakes AS q, area
  WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND time >= coalesce(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
AND time < coalesce(try_cast($quakeTo AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ) AND mag >= coalesce(try_cast($mag_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND mag < coalesce(try_cast($mag_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) >= coalesce(try_cast($depth_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) < coalesce(try_cast($depth_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
)
SELECT round(max(mag), 1) AS "Strongest" FROM f

spec.title: People within 100 km
spec.description: People living in towns and cities within 100 km of the filtered earthquakes of magnitude 4.5 or more. Counted from Natural Earth's populated places (city proper, not metro areas), so it leaves out rural areas: read it as a lower bound.

spec.rawSql:
WITH area AS (
  SELECT
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
  FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($quakeArea, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
), f AS (
  SELECT q.* FROM $quakes AS q, area
  WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND time >= coalesce(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
AND time < coalesce(try_cast($quakeTo AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ) AND mag >= coalesce(try_cast($mag_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND mag < coalesce(try_cast($mag_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) >= coalesce(try_cast($depth_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) < coalesce(try_cast($depth_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
)
SELECT coalesce(sum(e.people_100km), 0) AS "People within 100 km" FROM f LEFT JOIN $exposure AS e ON e.id = f.id

WITH area AS (
  SELECT
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
  FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($quakeArea, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
), f AS (
  SELECT q.* FROM $quakes AS q, area
  WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND time >= coalesce(try_cast($quakeFrom AS TIMESTAMPTZ), '-infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ)
AND time < coalesce(try_cast($quakeTo AS TIMESTAMPTZ), 'infinity'::TIMESTAMPTZ) AND mag >= coalesce(try_cast($mag_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND mag < coalesce(try_cast($mag_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) >= coalesce(try_cast($depth_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) < coalesce(try_cast($depth_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
)
SELECT f.place AS "Place",
       round(f.mag, 1) AS "Magnitude",
       coalesce(f.alert, 'none') AS "PAGER alert",
       CASE WHEN f.tsunami = 1 THEN 'yes' ELSE '' END AS "Tsunami",
       e.people_100km AS "People within 100 km",
       e.largest_place AS "Largest place",
       e.largest_pop AS "Its population",
       f.id, f.latitude, f.longitude
FROM f JOIN $exposure AS e ON e.id = f.id
WHERE e.people_100km > 0
ORDER BY e.people_100km DESC
LIMIT 10

spec.title: Earthquakes per day
spec.description: Every earthquake per day in grey, and those the magnitude, depth and area filters leave in colour. It ignores the map's time slider: this is the month the slider moves through.

spec.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(time, 1d) AS time, count(*) AS "All" FROM $quakes WHERE $__timeFilter(time) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH area AS (
  SELECT
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 1) AS xs,
    list_filter(n, lambda v, i: i % 2 = 0) AS ys
  FROM (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract_all($quakeArea, '-?[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?') AS DOUBLE[]) AS n)
)
SELECT $__timeGroup(time, 1d) AS time, count(*) AS "Filtered"
FROM $quakes, area
WHERE $__timeFilter(time) AND mag >= coalesce(try_cast($mag_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND mag < coalesce(try_cast($mag_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) >= coalesce(try_cast($depth_lo AS DOUBLE), '-infinity'::DOUBLE)
AND greatest(least(depth, 299.9), 0) < coalesce(try_cast($depth_hi AS DOUBLE), 'infinity'::DOUBLE) AND (len(area.xs) = 0 OR list_sum(list_transform(range(1, len(area.xs) + 1), lambda i:
  CASE WHEN (area.ys[i] > latitude) <> (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] > latitude)
        AND longitude < (area.xs[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.xs[i]) * (latitude - area.ys[i]) / (area.ys[i % len(area.xs) + 1] - area.ys[i]) + area.xs[i]
       THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) % 2 = 1)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

options.content:
**Click an earthquake** on the map, or a row in *Most exposed*, to see who lives near it.

**Drag** across the magnitude or depth bars, **draw** an area on the map, or move the map's **time slider**: every panel follows, answered in your browser.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT q.place AS "Place",
       strftime(q.time AT TIME ZONE 'UTC', '%d %b %H:%M UTC') AS "Time",
       round(q.mag, 1) AS "Magnitude",
       round(q.depth) AS "Depth (km)",
       coalesce(q.alert, 'none') AS "PAGER alert",
       q.mmi AS "Intensity (MMI)",
       q.felt AS "Felt reports",
       CASE WHEN q.tsunami = 1 THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS "Tsunami",
       e.people_100km AS "People within 100 km",
       q.url AS url
FROM $quakes AS q
LEFT JOIN $exposure AS e ON e.id = q.id
WHERE q.id = $quake

WITH q AS (SELECT latitude, longitude FROM $quakes WHERE id = $quake),
     candidates AS (
       SELECT p.name AS "Place", p.country AS "Country", p.pop_min AS "Population",
              round(2 * 6371 * asin(sqrt(
                power(sin(radians(p.latitude - q.latitude) / 2), 2)
                + cos(radians(q.latitude)) * cos(radians(p.latitude))
                  * power(sin(radians(p.longitude - q.longitude) / 2), 2)))) AS km
       FROM q, $places AS p
       WHERE p.latitude BETWEEN q.latitude - 1 AND q.latitude + 1
     )
SELECT "Place", "Country", "Population", km AS "Distance (km)"
FROM candidates
WHERE km <= 100
ORDER BY "Population" DESC
LIMIT 15

options.content:
### Where the data comes from

- **Earthquakes**: the [USGS real-time feed](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/feed/v1.0/geojson.php) of the last 30 days, read straight from USGS by your browser when the dashboard opens. *PAGER alert*, *intensity (MMI)*, *felt reports* and *tsunami* are USGS's own assessments, published only for the earthquakes that warrant one.
- **Populated places**: [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) 1:10m populated places (v5.1.2), about 7,300 towns and cities with population estimates. Public domain.

### How "people within 100 km" is counted

For every earthquake of magnitude 4.5 or more, the populations of the Natural Earth places within 100 km of the epicentre are added up. It uses each place's city-proper figure, not its metropolitan area, so a metro area listed as several places is not counted twice. It leaves out everyone living outside those places, so **read it as a lower bound**, not as USGS's PAGER exposure estimate.

### How it works

Both datasets are loaded once into DuckDB running in your browser (the Chaski data source). Every filter and click is answered there, without a round trip to the server.
